correctness.rationale: For every finite Boolean vertex set, the Euclidean projection of the cube midpoint onto its convex hull gives the unique minimum-enclosing center: the Boolean norm identity converts squared distance to a linear functional, projection supplies its sharp supporting face, and every competing center costs an additional squared displacement. The standard matroid rank inequality system then makes the sharp uniform-matroid envelope an if-and-only-if feasibility problem. For rank below half, feasibility is exactly uniform density; at and above half rank, Edmonds partition is exactly the half-vector feasibility criterion. Contact sets follow from the same supporting functional, and the strict/quantitative deficit from the projection Pythagorean inequality and rank-constraint Cauchy bound. Direct-sum sharpness is computed exactly. Numerical replay on finite families is corroborative only.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural metric classification of when any finite matroid independence polytope attains the maximum possible minimum-enclosing Euclidean radius given only rank and size. The two equality classes are mathematically different and significant existing matroid notions—uniform density versus arboricity at most two—whose geometric sphere meanings and distinct vertex-contact phases are identified. It also gives an exact variational formula, a new quantitative rank-obstruction deficit with a sharp example, and explicit nonuniform graphic matroid attainments. These are not arbitrary small instances or bare restatements of the earlier uniform polytope special case, though the proof efficiently combines established structural ingredients.
